# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

insights.line: What made the others more pressing?

whys.g1: Both answers say the same thing a super would say — subs not showing up and the schedule slipping matter more than the log — and the group name says it plainly.
whys.g2: There is no junk or off-topic answer on this line, so nothing junk was grouped.

founder.order_why: It runs from naming and market, to the context and recall window, to the problem's prevalence, frequency, other difficulties and current way, to who asks and who gets a link, which is how I'd explain Fresco to a stranger.
founder.asked_twice: Screens 3 and 5 carry the same kicker and question ('Before we test anything, let's define exactly where this idea applies.') on either side of the window question, so they read as the same context screen shown twice.
founder.missing: Nothing in the flow asks about the solution (narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC), the price ($1k per site per month), or who pays (the general contractor, per site, not the superintendent), so the buyer side of my company never comes up.

PRIMARY.order_why: Asking which part I'd most like made easier comes before asking how my last log actually went, so I'm picking a wish before I've walked back through the day; and screens 1 and 2 both say 1 of 4.
PRIMARY.missing: Nothing about the photos, which is the real time sink: getting the day's site photos uploaded into Procore and tied to the log entries. Also nothing on how long the log took me, or whether I'd needed those logs later for a delay dispute with the owner.

screens.why7: All five rungs sit on one measure, time to get the log written; the first is today's way working, the last is outright failure, and the line under the first leaves rungs both for and against with a fitting escape.
screens.instead: For most construction superintendents, typing up the daily log after the walk still falls short.

screens.why1: Just before the link goes to supers, it makes sense to choose who asks the questions on the video, and nothing here repeats an earlier screen.
screens.why2: The question and the hint are plain: voice on video, text on screen as a fallback, 400 credits either way, and the link goes out by text, which is how my supers live anyway.
screens.why3: Picking which voice my own study goes out in is my call and needs nothing I don't know.
screens.why4: Two voices with a 5-second sample are distinct and complete enough, but the bare names don't say accent or tone, and for US superintendents I'd want to know which one sounds like a plain American voice before I have to tap through both.
screens.why5: Nothing of my problem, product or roles is reworded here, and the screen leaks nothing about Fresco to the respondent.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions? Options: Daphne (US English, calm) ▶ Hear · 5 s / Saskia (US English, brisk) ▶ Hear · 5 s, with the same hint on credits and the text-message link.

screens.why1: Right after choosing who asks the questions, deciding how supers answer is the obvious next step before sending.
screens.why2: Plain words; 'AI interviewer', 'read and tap', 'speak into it or type' are clear to me as a founder building an AI scribe.
screens.why3: I know my supers -- in the trailer at end of day on a phone, short on time -- so I can judge whether they'd tap or talk to Daphne.
screens.why4: Three distinct, complete choices (video AI, text, let them pick) with no overlap and nothing missing.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product or roles leaks; it just uses my audience's name, construction superintendents, as I typed it.

screens.why1: After choosing how supers answer, deciding who gets the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: The choices read plainly, though "People I found with Keel -- From a search on the Contacts page" means nothing to me until I've seen that page, and "signs in with Google" is fine but a little out of place.
screens.why3: I know which supers I can reach: the ones I've walked sites with in Napa and the South Bay, plus intros from GCs, so I can answer this from my own situation.
screens.why4: The three routes are distinct and cover how I'd reach supers, but the second option's 'Pick a list' is written in Keel's voice rather than the 'I...' voice of the other two, so it reads unevenly.
screens.why5: Nothing of Fresco's product or its roles shows up here, and my pick, people I know by name, is kept.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? -- People I know by name (I send each their own link) / People I pick from a Keel search (Keel makes a link for each; I send them) / A group, one open link (I post it where supers already are, like a GC's channel or a super forum)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits beside 'Frequency: 4 counted', but the threshold of 5 isn't there, and naming only Frequency when Importance and Current solution are also short makes me wonder why that one decides it.
screens.why_b2: The page draws no chart, and the tally is plain, but it is printed twice; the kicker's '4 TO 7 COUNTED' made me look again before I saw that three of my four cards each lost three of the seven.
screens.why_b3: Prevalence, Frequency and Current solution are my beliefs in my words, but the Importance line reads like Keel's machinery ('have five things that are hard when...') rather than how I'd say the daily log is one of a super's two worst chores.
screens.why_b4: '4 counted · 5 needed' implies I need more supers counted, but nothing says how many more to recruit, why three of seven dropped out of the count, or what the one holding belief means for Fresco.
screens.why_b5: The page claims nothing past the seven who answered: n is in the kicker and the tally, Prevalence at exactly 6 of 7 is called 'holding up' and 'at the bar' rather than strong, and the short cards say they are too few.
screens.instead: Too few to call: three of four beliefs have 4 of the 5 supers they need (three of seven answered too vaguely to count); get at least one more superintendent's clear answer on Frequency, Importance and Current solution. The daily log is near-universal (6 of 7, just at the bar).

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Holding up' sits right beside '6 of 7 said yes · bar 6 of 7 · at the bar', so I see both the call and the number that decides it.
screens.why_b2: The strip shows 6 for and 1 against over an axis of 0 to 7, with my bar marked at 6 and labelled 'at least 8 in 10', so what is counted, over how many, and where the bar sits are plain at once.
screens.why_b3: I recognise it, but my belief was about supers typing up the log after their site walks, on commercial jobs; 'typed site notes into the daily log' drops both, and that is what every super does anyway, which is why Denise, who logs as she goes, counts for me.
screens.why_b4: It points me to the next two cards, but it doesn't say what this means for Fresco: whether the pain I'm selling, the after-walk typing in the trailer, is common, or only that logging is.
screens.why_b5: n is visible and 'a lean, not a call' is said, but 'Holding up' at the bar exactly on 7 people, from a gate almost any super would say yes to, reads firmer than the data carries: one more No would flip it.
screens.instead: Exactly at your bar on 7: 6 of 7 typed notes into the log, but the question didn't ask if they typed it up after the walk, so this shows logging is universal, not that the end-of-day typing is; one more No and it fails.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both, so I know where I stand and why.
screens.why_b2: The x-axis (working days out of 5) and '4 counted' are plain, but the bar needs a second look: 'your bar · 4 of 5 (at least 2 in 3)' mixes my low of 4 days with the 5 people needed, the axis runs from 0 though nobody could answer 0, and the legend's 'short of it' marks nothing here.
screens.why_b3: 'Type site notes into the daily log on 4 to 5 working days out of 5' is my range in my trade's words, and the card is titled Frequency as I checked it.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it does not tell me that one more counted answer calls it, or that every count so far is at my bar.
screens.why_b5: It is careful about the small group ('a lean, not a call'), but the tag '— the most recent time it happened' misdescribes a count-over-5-days question, and 'your bar · 4 of 5' can read as a result rather than the threshold.
screens.instead: Leaning your way, not yet a call: all 4 who gave a count typed notes into the log on 5 of 5 days (Hank declined, Luis guessed); one more counted answer decides it.

screens.why_b1: The status 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict and exactly why.
screens.why_b2: The bars plainly count 8 picks from 4 people, and my row is marked as the one I named, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' next to '4 counted' took me a second look to read as 'need 4 for out of 5' rather than a count of who answered.
screens.why_b3: Importance and the line about sorting photos and typing notes into the daily log, among the things hard after the walks, is my belief in my own words.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic; it doesn't tell me to get one more super counted, or that both against picked schedule and subs, which is the thing I'd act on.
screens.why_b5: n is visible and the small group is flagged, but 'a lean, not a call' implies a direction when the split is 2 for and 2 against, a dead tie.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of 4 put the log in their two, 2 chose schedule and subs instead. One more super counted decides it; ask whether the schedule, not the log, is what eats their day.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside its deciding number, '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', and the So line repeats both.
screens.why_b2: The rungs with their counts and the line under 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk' read at once, but the strip's 'your bar · 4 of 5' with a ghost cell, when only 4 were counted, takes a second look to work out that the bar assumes a fifth person.
screens.why_b3: Current solution, and the act 'typing up the daily log in the trailer' with my own rungs from half an hour to never written up that day, are my words for my supers' evening in the trailer.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't say that 3 of the 4 counted fell short or that one more counted super (say, getting Hank or Luis a straight answer) would decide it.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible (6 answered, 4 counted, who was dropped and why), the small group is called 'a lean, not a call', and nothing claims the belief held.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of the 4 counted fell short of 'Typed up within half an hour of the walk' (2 took a couple of hours, 1 the rest of the evening), so it leans your way; one more counted super decides it.

screens.why_b1: The status word 'Too few to call' sits beside '4 counted · 5 needed to call it', so I know there is no verdict yet and which number keeps it open.
screens.why_b3: Importance and the belief about sorting photos and typing notes into the daily log being one of the two difficulties they most want made easier are the words I checked.
screens.why_b4: '5 needed to call it' implies I need one more counted answer, but nothing says what two of four against means for the idea, such as whether to reposition the log next to schedule and subs work.
screens.why_b5: The n stays visible (4 counted, 2 against, 2 asked) and the low n is named rather than dressed up as a lean either way.
screens.why_b6: Denise finishing her log on the tablet before the gate, and Ray saying 'the log can wait till morning, the deck can't', tell me the log is deferrable while subs and the schedule are not, which is a threat to my urgency story I did not type.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 2 of the 4 counted put subs and the schedule above the log, saying the log can wait and the schedule can't; get one more answer, and test whether Fresco's texting of action items to the crew is the hook rather than the log itself.

screens.why1: As the first screen it makes sense to check whether my job is on Procore or ACC before asking anything about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Procore and ACC are what my company and every GC I know run jobs on, so I read it once and answer.
screens.why3: I know which platform my current job is set up in; I'm in it every day.
screens.why4: Yes or No covers it cleanly for a set-up fact, and a gate rightly carries no escape.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's segment of jobs on Procore or ACC, and nothing about their product shows.
screens.why6: It's short and spoken as one question, and ACC is said the way supers say it, letter by letter, then yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my job runs on Procore or ACC, asking about my daily log this week is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Site notes and daily log are my words, and I'd answer it the first time I heard it.
screens.why3: I know exactly whether I typed notes into the log this week, because I do it every day.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it cleanly, and the chips belong to the story box after a Yes, not to the gate.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but dropping 'after your site walks' loses the part that hurts, which is typing it all up later instead of on the walk.
screens.why6: It is one short question with 'Yes or no' after it, so it is easy to answer by ear.
screens.why7: Every working super types notes into the daily log, so this asks the routine, not the problem; nobody can truly say No, and the belief can never be refuted.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you type up the daily log after your site walks? Yes · No

screens.why1: Right after I said yes to typing notes into the daily log this week, asking how many days I did it is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log and site notes are exactly what I call them on a Procore job, so I can answer on first hearing.
screens.why3: I know which days I got my notes into the log this week and which ones slid, so this is straight from my own week.
screens.why4: One button per working day from 1 to 5 covers every true answer for someone who already said yes, and I can't recall fits as the escape.
screens.why5: It asks about my own daily log in my own trade's words, with nothing about anybody's product or plan showing through.
screens.why6: It is one short question and a number from 1 to 5, which I can hear once and answer without thinking about it.
screens.why7: The options are all on one measure, working days out of 5, running from 1 up to 5 with no 0 and no bands, the unit is said once in the window phrase, the act is a seven-word thing done on a given day, and I can't recall is the one escape; whether the belief can be refuted depends on a founder's low I was not shown.

screens.why1: I just told it I type site notes into the log most days, so asking which after-walk chore I'd most want easier follows naturally.
screens.why2: Subs, RFIs, the schedule, the daily log are all my words, though "your last day of site walks" reads a touch odd since I walk the site every day; "your last day on site" is how I'd say it.
screens.why3: Every one of these is something I do myself at the end of the day after walking the job, so I can answer from what I did yesterday.
screens.why4: The five are distinct jobs I actually juggle, none swallows another, the photos-and-notes row is one chore to me because the photos are the notes, and None of these fits.
screens.why5: Nothing hints at a product or a company's idea; it just lists my own end-of-day chores in my words.
screens.why6: One short question and five short phrases read as a list I can hold, with the escape said last; the photos-and-notes row is the longest but still says fine.
screens.why7: One measure (most like made easier), the founder's own row about sorting photos and typing notes into the daily log is present and not first, four rivals from my own part of the work at that moment let it be refuted or supported, and None of these sits at the first ask.
screens.instead: Think of your last day on site. Which one of these would you most like made easier? Following up on safety issues from the walk; lining up subs for tomorrow; updating the schedule after the walk; sorting photos and typing notes into the daily log; writing up RFIs from the walk; or none of these.

screens.why1: After asking which part of the day's site walks I'd most like made easier, asking how my last daily log write-up actually went is the obvious next question.
screens.why2: Daily log, the walk and the trailer are my everyday words, though saying 'daily log' twice in two sentences is clunky.
screens.why3: I write the log myself most days and know how long it took last time, even if some nights I finish it in the truck or at home rather than the trailer.
screens.why4: The options mix two things: 'within half an hour of the walk' and 'a couple of hours after the walk' read as when I got to it, while 'took about an hour' reads as how long it took, so a day where I started late but finished quickly could fit two of them.
screens.why5: Nothing about a product or the founder's plan comes through; it is just my log and my time.
screens.why6: Heard once, it is one short question and five short parallel options I can hold, with the escape said last.
screens.why7: There is a working rung first and an outright failure last, five in order, and the right escape, but the measure bends between delay after the walk and time spent typing, which edges toward the card's 'when the log was finished' stand-in.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. How long did typing it up take? Under half an hour · About an hour · A couple of hours · Most of the evening · Never got written up that day · Someone else did it
